local_verification_required: Windows installed app (coordinator, deferred native access): first run → Open folder as library via the Windows folder picker → second library → switch/rename/remove/re-add → restart restores; app-data under the Windows known-folder location with proper isolation (not APPDATA override).
Windows path handling: drive-letter and UNC paths, case-insensitive dedupe (canonical key lowercases on Windows, strips \\?\), a library on a removable/disconnected drive shown as 'Folder not found'.
Windows upgrade of an existing single-library install on a backed-up copy: library listed, positions/highlights/vault kept, library.db unchanged, previous build still opens it.
WebView2 keyboard/focus behaviour of the Libraries dialog (Escape, Tab trap, focus return to switcher).
review_walkthrough: Fresh app-data → Libraries page with no library and an empty path field → Open folder as library… → pick folder A → 'Indexed N books' (C1).
Tab-rail switcher → Libraries dialog → Open folder as library… → folder B → B opens; dialog lists A and B with path and count; adding A again (any spelling) does not duplicate (C1).
Read a book in A, switch to B: B has no A tabs/progress/highlights; Obsidian: B cannot use A's folder (C3).
Rename B, Remove from list (read the explanation), add B's folder again → same name and progress (C2).
Quit, move A's folder, relaunch → 'Folder not found … Nothing was opened in its place' → Locate folder… → A reopens with its progress (C4).
known_risks: A switch that fails after the workspace was closed (e.g. folder vanished in between) reopens the previous library with its reader tabs closed; the error is shown.

Late writes from the previous library get up to 1.5 s to finish before switching; a write issued later is refused (never redirected), so an unflushed position older than that can be lost, as when closing a tab.
Obsidian vault path must now be an existing folder (previously created on export).

assetProtocol.scope is ['**'] (pre-existing): the webview can load any local file by path. Narrowing it per library is a security-sensitive capability change not made here; recommended as a separate decision.
Nested libraries are refused by design (each library indexes everything under its folder); owner may prefer allowing them.
